design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a double-blinded randomized controlled trial in which 44 participants were randomly allocated to either the probiotic soy milk or conventional soy milk group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors state participants were randomly allocated, but provide no details on sequence generation or allocation concealment methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 44 participants were randomly allocated to the soy milk group (control) or probiotic soy milk group who received 200 mL/d of soy milk or probiotic soy milk for 8 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blinded with identical-appearing bottles of soy milk, adherence was monitored by empty bottle counts and serum genistein, and no substantial deviations from the intended protocol were apparent.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At each study visit, participants received sufficient bottles of soy milk for a 3-day period until the next visit, in a doubleblinded design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 4 of 44 participants (9%) dropped out with balanced numbers and similar reasons across groups, making bias due to missing data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Forty-four patients participated, and 40 completed the study (20 patients in each group; Figure). Two men in the probiotic group were excluded because of hospitalization (n = 1) and loss to follow-up (n = 1). One man and 1 woman in the control group were also excluded due to poor adherence and loss to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory-based biochemical measurements conducted in a blinded manner using standard automated analyzers and assays.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All the tests were performed in a blinded fashion, in pairs (before and after the intervention) at the same time, in the same analytic run, and in random order to reduce systematic error and interassay variability.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was prospectively registered in a clinical trial registry and reported predefined primary and secondary kidney function endpoints consistently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study protocol was registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (Register code: IRCT201601027479N2 available at: http://www.irct.ir).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of detailed reporting regarding the sequence generation and allocation concealment methods in Domain 1, despite robust blinding, low attrition, and objective outcome assessment across other domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where participants were allocated to groups using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although computer-generated random numbers were used, there is no mention of allocation concealment methods (such as sequentially numbered sealed opaque envelopes or central allocation).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was carried out using computer-generated random numbers by a trained staf member at the internal clinic. At the onset of the study, to decrease potential confounding efects, stratified randomization of all participants was performed according to age, BMI, gender and the dosage and kind of medication (antidiabetic and antilipidemic agents, and insulin therapy).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical placebo packaging, minimizing deviations from intervention, and an intention-to-treat approach was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The placebo group received capsules in similar shape and packaging as the probiotic. ... The analyses were done based on the intention-to-treat approach (ITT). The missing values were treated based on the Last-Observation-Carried-Forward (LOCF) method.

domain_judgments.rationale: Dropouts were low (10% overall, 3 per group) and balanced between groups, and an intention-to-treat analysis using LOCF was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the patients in the probiotic group, 3 patients [withdrawn due to personal reasons (n = 3)], and in the placebo group, 3 persons [withdrawn due to personal reasons (n = 3)] were excluded (Fig. 1). Finally, 54 participants [probiotic (n = 27) and placebo (n = 27)] completed the trial. However, as the analysis was done based on the ITT principle, all 60 people (30 in each group) were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and biochemical measurements evaluated with commercial kits and standard formulas, and blinding was maintained.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the baseline and end-of-treatment, 15 mL blood samples were obtained from each patient at the Kashan reference laboratory in the early morning after an overnight fast. Available commercial kits were used to determine fasting plasma glucose (FPG), lipid profiles, creatinine, BUN and urine protein concentrations (Pars Azmun, Tehran, Iran).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (IRCT2017061134458N1) and outcomes reported align with the specified primary and secondary outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial with homeostasis model of assessment-estimated insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) as the primary and other metabolic profiles, and biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress as the secondary outcomes. ... This clinical trial was registered by the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (http://www.irct.ir: # IRCT2017061134458N1).

overall_summary: The trial is generally well-conducted and double-blinded, but lacks information on allocation concealment during the randomization process, leading to an overall judgment of some concerns.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where participants were randomly allocated to either probiotic or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation sequence concealment is reported ('None of the subjects involved in the study had access to the allocation sequence until the end of the statistical analyses'), the method of manual sequence generation is not described in detail, raising some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The random sequence of treatment (probiotic and placebo) was manually generated for a simple randomization. None of the subjects involved in the study had access to the allocation sequence until the end of the statistical analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical capsules and no indication of unintended interventions or protocol deviations that would bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants and the researchers who interviewed and visited the subjects were blinded to the contents of the bottles, which contained probiotic or placebo capsules.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial attrition occurred (13/46, ~28% missing), and the analysis was restricted to completers (complete-case analysis) without imputation or sensitivity analysis to address potential bias from missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Seven patients in the probiotic group and 6 in the placebo group left the study (Fig. 1). ... Sixteen patients remained in the probiotic group ... and 17 in the placebo group

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and biochemical measurements evaluated in a centralized laboratory in a blinded manner.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All laboratory measurements were centralized and performed in a blinded manner.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis protocol is reported, and multiple tests/metrics (within-group changes vs. delta percentage between groups) were analyzed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The differences of the variable were analyzed using nonparametric tests (paired tests, Wilcoxon) or parametric tests (Independent Samples t-test or Paired Samples t-test). The percentage delta (D) was also used to check the differences in the variables before and after supplementation.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by high risk in missing outcome data due to substantial attrition (~28% overall dropouts) analyzed with complete-case methods, alongside some concerns regarding lack of trial pre-registration and vague details of manual sequence generation.

design_rationale: The study is described as a parallel randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial where participants were randomly assigned to probiotic or placebo groups using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computer-generated random sequence was used and allocation was described as hidden, baseline differences were observed in several biochemical variables (QUICKI, TAC, MDA, BUN, albumin) and the details of allocation concealment implementation are sparse.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization assignment was conducted using computergenerated random numbers. Randomization and allocation were hidden from the researchers and patients until the final analyses were completed. The randomized allocation sequence, enrolling participants and allocating them to interventions, was conducted by a trained nutritionist at the dialysis clinic.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical placebo capsules, participants and researchers were unaware of assignments, and an intention-to-treat analysis was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was a prospective randomized, double-blind, placebocontrolled clinical trial... However, because the analysis was done based on the intention-to-treat principle, all 60 participants (30 in each group) were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing data was low (5 of 60, 8.3%), balanced between groups, and all randomized participants were included in the ITT analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two participants in the probiotic group and 3 participants in the placebo group withdrew due to personal reasons, and were excluded from the study (Figure 1). Fifty-five participants (probiotic [n 28] and placebo [n 27]) completed the trial. However, because the analysis was done based on the intention-to-treat principle, all 60 participants (30 in each group) were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and biochemical measurements evaluated with standard commercial kits, and assessors/participants remained blinded to intervention assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization and allocation were hidden from the researchers and patients until the final analyses were completed... Before and after the end of the intervention, 10-ml blood samples were obtained from each patient after an overnight fast and before dialysis at the Akhavan Clinic laboratory.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered in a public clinical trial registry (IRCT), and results are reported according to pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes without indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The present study was approved by the ethics committee of KUMS and was registered in the Iranian website for clinical trials (http://www.irct.ir: IRCT201601025623N69).

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, driven by some concerns in Domain 1 regarding baseline imbalances across several biochemical parameters despite computer-generated randomization, while all other domains demonstrated low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial in which participants were randomly allocated to study groups using a random number table.

domain_judgments.rationale: While sequence generation used a random number table by an investigator not clinically involved, allocation concealment procedures (such as sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes or central allocation) were not explicitly described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was done using a random number table by one of the investigators who had no clinical involvement in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind using control honey, no deviations from intended interventions were noted, and an intention-to-treat approach analyzing all randomized patients was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial... The analyses were carried out based on intention-to-treat (ITT) principle... all 60 participants (30 in each group) were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was very low (3 out of 60, or 5%), balanced between groups, and all randomized participants were included in the reported ITT analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among patients in the probiotic honey group, two patients [withdrawn (n = 2)] and in the control honey group, one person [withdrawn (n = 1)] were excluded (Fig. 1). Finally, 57 participants [probiotic honey (n = 28) and control honey (n = 29)] completed the trial. However, as the analysis was done based on ITT principle, all 60 participants (30 in each group) were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory biomarkers evaluated using standard commercial assays and spectrophotometric/ELISA methods, unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Before the onset and after the end ofthe intervention, 10-mL fasting blood samples were obtained from each patient at Kashan reference laboratory. Available commercial kits were used to determine FPG, lipid profiles, creatinine, and BUN concentrations (Pars Azmun, Tehran, Iran)...

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (IRCT201705035623N115) and reported all pre-specified primary and secondary metabolic, inflammatory, and oxidative stress outcomes according to a standard analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcomes were parameters of insulin metabolism in the current study. Secondary outcome variables were fasting plasma glucose (FPG), lipid profiles, biomarkers ofinflammation, and oxidative stress, serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) concentrations.

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, driven by lack of explicit details regarding allocation concealment during the randomization process despite otherwise well-conducted double-blind procedures, minimal missing data, objective laboratory outcomes, and trial registration.
